violations.quote: It’s stronger than Raised Bed because it also contributes end‐game points rather than just flat food.
violations.rule: Raised Bed has printed 1 VP on play (card text shows “1 VP”), so it is not “just flat food.”

violations.quote: gives an extra plow on each farmland or cultivation action
violations.rule: Plow Hero’s effect triggers only when using Farmland or Cultivation with the first person you place in a round (card text), not on every such action.

violations.quote: enabling free plow actions
violations.rule: Seed Almanac lets you pay 1 Food to plow a field; the plow actions it grants are not free

violations.quote: it provides ongoing crop resources rather than just food
violations.rule: Field Caretaker’s clay→grain exchange happens only once when you play the card; it does not provide an ongoing resource effect

violations.quote: Store of Experience rewards you with free resources (stone, reed, clay, wood) as you play down your occupation cards
violations.rule: Store of Experience triggers only once, immediately when you play that Minor Improvement, based on occupations left in hand; it does not trigger on each occupation you later play

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher and Seed Almanac giving you free plow actions and fields
violations.rule: Barrow Pusher grants 1 clay and 1 food per new field tile but does not provide plow actions or free fields; Seed Almanac lets you pay 1 Food to plow a field after playing a Minor Improvement, so its plow actions are not free

violations.quote: Christianity provides 2 immediate VP with no setup requirement
violations.rule: Christianity requires exactly 1 Sheep to play (prerequisite) and only then grants its 2 VP and gives opponents food

violations.quote: Home Brewer converts every grain into 3 food or a point
violations.rule: Home Brewer lets you turn exactly 1 grain per harvest into 3 Food or 1 bonus point—not every grain.

violations.quote: Seed Almanac doubles down on plowing by granting free plow actions after minors, ensuring you can cycle fields rapidly.
violations.rule: Seed Almanac requires you to pay 1 Food to plow 1 Field after each Minor Improvement; it does not grant free plow actions.

violations.quote: Seed Almanac and Field Caretaker enable frequent plowing
violations.rule: Field Caretaker is a field tile but does not grant any plow actions or alter plow costs; it does not enable plowing.

violations.quote: turn every future Minor or Major Improvement into free food
violations.rule: Basketmaker's Workshop only allows converting up to 1 Reed to 2–3 Food per Harvest; it does not trigger on playing or drafting Improvements

violations.quote: fills the food gap by generating food each time you draft or play an MI
violations.rule: Basketmaker's Workshop does not generate food upon drafting or playing Improvements; it grants a conversion ability once per Harvest

violations.quote: Basket Weaver immediately builds the Basketmaker’s Workshop, which combines with Festival Planning to give repeated Minor Improvement actions and reeds to plow via Seed Almanac.
violations.rule: Basketmaker’s Workshop does not produce reeds; it converts Reed to Food and scores points, but never grants Reed.

violations.quote: Threshing Board grants a free Bake Bread action on every Farmland or Cultivation, pairing with Barrow Pusher and Field Caretaker to convert grain into high‐impact food.
violations.rule: Baking bread requires both a Bake Bread action and a Baking Improvement; without a Baking Improvement a Bake Bread action alone cannot convert grain into Food.

violations.quote: guaranteed vegetables each harvest
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker allows you to pay 2 Food to buy 1 Vegetable at the end of each Harvest; it does not grant free or guaranteed Vegetables

violations.quote: converting vegetables into extra harvest resources
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker does not convert Vegetables into Food or other resources; it merely allows you to buy Vegetables for Food

violations.quote: hitting 2+ grain triggers free food and bonus grain each harvest
violations.rule: Eternal Rye Cultivation gives 1 Food if you have exactly 2 Grain at Harvest and gives 1 Grain if you have 3 or more Grain; it does not grant both on 2+ Grain

violations.quote: Seed Almanac, Festival Planning, and Barn Cats provide spare plow and harvest actions.
violations.rule: Barn Cats does not grant any extra actions. It only places food tokens on future round spaces (1 food on each of the next 2/3/4/5 remaining rounds, depending on number of stables) as per its card text.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, Seed Almanac and Festival Planning all reward field placement and harvest triggers.
violations.rule: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, and Seed Almanac trigger on field placement or play, not on harvest; only Festival Planning triggers a harvest. Their card texts do not grant harvest‐triggered benefits.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher and Field Caretaker synergize to turn each new field into food, clay, and grain
violations.rule: Field Caretaker only triggers once on play as a one‐time exchange for grain, not for each new field, so it does not convert every new field into grain

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher and Field Caretaker provide rotating food and grain
violations.rule: Field Caretaker’s effect is a one‐time exchange on play, not a recurring trigger, so it does not provide rotating grain

violations.quote: Only minor free plow actions via Seed Almanac
violations.rule: Seed Almanac requires paying 1 Food to plow a field; it does not grant free plow actions

violations.quote: You lack plow-tagged improvements (Swing/Wheel Plow) to enhance plow actions
violations.rule: No Swing Plow or Wheel Plow improvements exist in the base game card pool

violations.quote: giving 2 food each work phase you place a field tile or improvement on your farmyard
violations.rule: Farmyard Worker triggers only when you place at least one good (resource) on a farmyard space, not when placing field tiles or improvements

violations.quote: you can buy for food at harvest
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker lets you buy exactly 1 vegetable by paying 2 food at the end of each harvest—it does not let you sell/buy vegetables for food

violations.quote: Seed Almanac and Barrow Pusher ensure plenty of plow capacity.
violations.rule: Barrow Pusher only grants 1 clay and 1 food for each new field tile; it does not grant additional plow actions or capacity.

violations.quote: Garden Claw … each extra planted field you’ll have increases the food placements
violations.rule: Garden Claw places 1 food on specific upcoming round spaces (rounds 5, 8, 10, 12) regardless of how many fields you have; it does not scale with planted fields.

violations.quote: Reed Belt … supplies the reeds needed for Seed Almanac’s plow triggers
violations.rule: Seed Almanac’s triggers require paying 1 food to plow a field, not reed; reed is not used for the Seed Almanac ability.

violations.quote: it pays on universal pasture actions rather than complex grain-to-veg conversions
violations.rule: Fellow Grazer scores bonus points during the scoring phase based on pastures covering at least three spaces; it does not trigger on any action.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Seed Almanac, Field Caretaker, Festival Planning, Bumper Crop and Winter Caretaker all push you to plow and sow many fields.
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker does not grant any plow or sow actions; it gives 1 grain when played and a vegetable-for-food trade at each harvest.

violations.quote: This occupation turns the fields you’ll plow and sow into scoring pastures: once you fence 3+ spaces of a field, you get 2 bonus points each.
violations.rule: Fellow Grazer scores 2 bonus points for each pasture you have covering at least 3 farmyard spaces; it does not refer to fencing ‘spaces of a field.’

violations.quote: It’s a more reliable floor than Pan Baker, which depends on having a Baking Hearth.
violations.rule: Pan Baker triggers on using the Grain Utilization action and does not require owning a Fireplace or Cooking Hearth.

violations.quote: Opponents have snapped up animal-breeding cards (Milking Stool) ...
violations.rule: Milking Stool grants food in harvest and scoring points for cattle; it does not affect animal breeding.

violations.quote: no cooking improvements to turn grain into food
violations.rule: Grain and Vegetables in the supply convert to 1 Food each at any time, no card needed

violations.quote: Without a cooking or animal engine, your grain will pile up but won’t feed your family, risking starvation or begging
violations.rule: Grain in supply converts to Food without any Improvement; cooking cards only improve rates

violations.quote: No cooking improvement or animal engine to convert grain/veg into late-game food
violations.rule: Grain and Vegetables convert to Food 1:1 automatically, no Improvement required

violations.quote: No Day Laborer, Stone House, or Traveling Players style engine to generate bonus actions
violations.rule: Day Laborer and Traveling Players provide Food only; Stone House Reconstruction grants a one-time Renovation action but neither Day Laborer nor Traveling Players give any actions

violations.quote: Multiple plow triggers from Barrow Pusher, Seed Almanac, Bumper Crop
violations.rule: Bumper Crop triggers the field phase, not a Plow action; it does not plow fields

violations.quote: synergizing with Barrow Pusher and Bumper Crop’s resource placements
violations.rule: Both Barrow Pusher and Bumper Crop give resources to your supply, not by placing goods on farmyard spaces, so they do not trigger Farmyard Worker

violations.quote: Festival Planning, Bumper Crop, and Seed Almanac provide extra plow/sow actions
violations.rule: Festival Planning and Bumper Crop trigger field phases (mini‐harvests), not plow or sow actions; only Seed Almanac grants a plow action

violations.quote: Reader guarantees a free room when you reach 7 occupations, directly addressing your missing growth/room gap without costing an action
violations.rule: Reader is an Occupation played on the Lessons action space, so it requires and costs that action

violations.quote: Tinsmith Master doubles your sow value by adding extra crops each field phase
violations.rule: Tinsmith Master grants exactly +1 crop per field sown, not a true doubling of the sow yield

violations.quote: requires only placing a good on your farmyard, which you already do with improvements
violations.rule: Farmyard Worker triggers only when you place actual resource goods (wood, clay, reed, grain, vegetables, animals) onto your farmyard spaces; playing improvements does not place resource goods and thus does not satisfy the trigger

violations.quote: "extra_actions": "Festival Planning, Bumper Crop, and Seed Almanac give repeat improvements and plow actions"
violations.rule: Bumper Crop does not grant a plow action—it only carries out the field phase (harvest) on your farmyard and gives no additional plow action

violations.quote: "plow": "Seed Almanac and Bumper Crop provide multiple free plow/harvest triggers"
violations.rule: Bumper Crop provides a field‐phase (harvest) trigger only; it does not plow fields, so it cannot provide free plow triggers

violations.quote: (1) It synergizes with Turnwrest Plow by multiplying your plow output on the Day Laborer action space
violations.rule: Turnwrest Plow’s effect triggers only when you use the Farmland or Cultivation action spaces, not Day Laborer

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, Seed Almanac, Festival Planning, and Bumper Crop all rewarding additional fields and sow actions.
violations.rule: Cards like Field Caretaker do not grant extra fields or sow actions—they only give grain when played and count as a field; they do not add plow or sow actions.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, Seed Almanac, Festival Planning, and Bumper Crop all rewarding additional fields and sow actions.
violations.rule: Seed Almanac grants additional Plow (fields) by paying Food when you play further Minors, but does not reward any Sow actions.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, Seed Almanac, Festival Planning, and Bumper Crop all rewarding additional fields and sow actions.
violations.rule: Festival Planning triggers a full field phase (sow) and Harvest but does not grant extra Plow or sow actions beyond carrying out those phases.

violations.quote: Barrow Pusher, Field Caretaker, Seed Almanac, Festival Planning, and Bumper Crop all rewarding additional fields and sow actions.
violations.rule: Bumper Crop triggers only the field phase (sow) and explicitly is not a Harvest; it does not grant extra fields or a Harvest phase.

violations.quote: Tinsmith Master doubles your sow yield
violations.rule: Tinsmith Master gives exactly +1 crop per field sown—not a doubling of the normal sow yield (3 → 4 grain or 2 → 3 vegetables).

violations.quote: Publican turns each opponent’s sow into a point
violations.rule: Publican gives you 1 bonus point only if you first give that opponent 1 Grain before their unconditional Sow action; it is not a free point per sow.

violations.quote: Festival Planning and Bumper Crop give extra sow and harvest-phase actions
violations.rule: Bumper Crop does not trigger a Harvest phase—it only carries out the field (sow) phase—so it does not provide an extra Harvest-phase action.

violations.quote: Synergizes with Feed Pellets by giving early sheep for pastures and tap-in fence actions
violations.rule: Animal Husbandry Worker does not grant any sheep; it only gives wood and a “Build Fences” action when played under the 3/6/9 rounds-left condition

violations.quote: Food Pellets plus Profiteering will cover round‐4 harvest.
violations.rule: Neither Feed Pellets nor Profiteering provide food during the Feeding phase: Feed Pellets trades a Vegetable for an Animal and Profiteering exchanges building resources, neither yielding Food; therefore they cannot cover feeding costs.

violations.quote: (2) it fills the current gap in raw goods supply to power your Day Laborer actions and future improvements
violations.rule: The Day Laborer action space yields 2 Food and has no resource cost, so providing raw goods does not 'power' Day Laborer actions; Day Laborer requires no input resources.

violations.quote: House Steward grants 2–4 wood on play based on rounds remaining
violations.rule: House Steward actually grants 1/2/3/4 wood depending on how many complete rounds remain (it can grant as little as 1 wood)

violations.quote: Feed Pellets and Profiteering’s 1 food provide early feeding support
violations.rule: Feed Pellets does not provide food or reduce feeding costs; it gives you an animal and allows exchanging a vegetable for an animal—it does not help you feed your family.

violations.quote: its one‐time investment scales with up to 9 uses
violations.rule: Collector’s action space can be used only four times (1st–4th), yielding 6/7/8/9 goods; there are not nine uses.

violations.quote: Treegardener’s harvest wood is less flexible and dependent on vegetable feeding
violations.rule: Treegardener triggers in the field phase of each harvest, giving wood regardless of vegetables—it is not tied to vegetable feeding.

violations.quote: giving a free "Family Growth Even without Room" action
violations.rule: Seducer requires paying 1 stone, 1 grain, 1 vegetable, and 1 sheep to take a "Family Growth Even without Room" action

violations.quote: any Grain Seeds visit becomes an opportunity for a free occupation play
violations.rule: Private Teacher’s text states you may play an occupation for an occupation cost of 1 food when it triggers; it is not free

violations.quote: using the stone and wood you’ll accumulate to unlock Bake Bread
violations.rule: Iron Oven costs 3 Stone (no Wood) to play; Wood is not required to acquire or use the Iron Oven

violations.quote: Roof Ballaster turns your future room count into a stone engine, letting you trade 1 food per room for stone.
violations.rule: Roof Ballaster’s text: “When you play this card, you can immediately pay 1 food to get 1 stone for each room you have.” It is a one‐time effect on play, not an ongoing engine.

violations.quote: Feed Pellets (which needs fenced pastures to keep sheep)
violations.rule: You may keep exactly 1 animal of any type as a pet in your house free of room or pasture; fenced pastures are only required once you exceed the 1‐pet limit.

violations.quote: Collector is the only extra‐action source and is one‐and‐done
violations.rule: Collector can be used up to 4 times (1st/2nd/3rd/4th use), not just once; it provides multiple extra actions.

violations.quote: No cards generate actions outside of your workers
violations.rule: Collector text: “This card is an action space for you only.” It gives you its own action outside the normal worker placements.

violations.quote: No reliable scaling food engine beyond Profiteering’s conversions and Feed Pellets
violations.rule: Profiteering only lets you exchange one building resource for another, it does not convert anything into food.

violations.quote: Profiteering and Assistant Tiller will deliver food
violations.rule: Assistant Tiller does not grant any food; it grants an extra plow on Day Laborer actions, and Profiteering only grants 1 food on play and thereafter allows exchanging building resources, not food.

violations.quote: You have only Collector for non-worker actions
violations.rule: Established Person also grants a non-worker action (Build Fences) immediately after renovation, so Collector is not the only source of extra actions.

violations.quote: Profiteering and Feed Pellets give some early food
violations.rule: Feed Pellets gives 1 sheep on play and has no immediate food effect

violations.quote: Debt Security helps free up actions for food later
violations.rule: Debt Security only awards bonus points during final scoring and has no effect on actions or food

violations.quote: Clay Kneader … only provides wood+clay over time and demands contested seed actions
violations.rule: Clay Kneader also immediately grants 1 wood and 2 clay when played; its time-based effect is only the additional clay on seed actions

violations.quote: House Steward ... by supplying wood each round to build your two-room clay house and then renovate
violations.rule: House Steward gives wood only once upon play based on rounds remaining, not each round

violations.quote: No dedicated food engine or recurrence beyond Hauberg and Profiteering
violations.rule: Hauberg places wood and wild boar on future rounds, not food; it is not a food engine

violations.quote: Collector provides a unique action space but no additional engine beyond one-off
violations.rule: Collector yields goods up to four times when used and serves as a recurring engine, not a single one-off

violations.quote: Feed Pellets supply trickle food
violations.rule: Feed Pellets gives animals (exchange vegetables for animals), not food; it does not supply food.

violations.quote: Profiteering supply trickle food
violations.rule: Profiteering gives 1 food only once on play and otherwise exchanges resources; it does not provide a recurring food trickle.

violations.quote: Hauberg supply trickle food
violations.rule: Hauberg places wood and wild boar on future round spaces, not food; it does not supply a food trickle.

violations.quote: House Steward supplies 1–4 wood each round
violations.rule: House Steward gives a one-time wood bonus on play based on rounds remaining, not wood each round.

violations.quote: Stockman turns every stable you build into immediate livestock
violations.rule: Stockman only gives animals on your 2nd, 3rd, and 4th stable builds, not every stable.

violations.quote: Assistant Tiller and Profiteering cover plowing via Day Laborer actions
violations.rule: Only Assistant Tiller provides an extra plow; Profiteering does not grant any plowing ability.

violations.quote: Priest enables early renovation for growth
violations.rule: Priest grants resources if in a clay house but does not allow renovation; it does not enable renovation.

violations.quote: These cards all hinge on a free renovation to exactly two rooms, unlocking stable builds and free resources.
violations.rule: Established Person gives a free renovation and a Build Fences action; Priest does not renovate; only Mining Hammer grants free stable builds when you renovate.

violations.quote: Combines with Established Person and Priest’s free two-room renovation to stone
violations.rule: Priest grants resources but does not renovate; only Established Person renovates.

violations.quote: Generates 2 clay and 2 stone every work phase
violations.rule: Freemason grants 2 clay if in a clay house or 2 stone if in a stone house, not both each phase.

violations.quote: Universally builds a food cache on all remaining rounds
violations.rule: Forest Well places 1 food on each remaining round space only up to the amount of wood in your supply.

violations.quote: requires only plowing some fields—no vegetable engine required
violations.rule: Crack Weeder’s harvest-phase bonus triggers only when you take vegetables from a field, so you need a vegetable engine to supply vegetables.

violations.quote: Established Person and Priest set up a free early renovation into stone
violations.rule: Priest does not perform or waive a renovation; it only grants resources (3 clay, 2 reed, 2 stone) when played and does not renovate the house

violations.quote: No scalable food engine drafted—only one‐off food from Profiteering and Hauberg
violations.rule: Hauberg places wood and wild boar on future round spaces; it does not provide any food

violations.quote: Open Air Farmer supports your early farm layout by giving two new spaces for just one worker and two wood.
violations.rule: Open Air Farmer also requires you to remove exactly 3 stables from your supply to build the pasture, not just 2 wood.

violations.quote: Wheel Plow enhances every Farmland or Cultivation action you’ll take by plowing three fields in a single worker
violations.rule: Wheel Plow triggers only once per game (and only on the first person placed), not on every placement.

violations.quote: Beer Table pairs with grain you’ll sow or buy later to deliver 2 bonus points at each harvest.
violations.rule: Beer Table requires paying 1 grain each time to gain 2 bonus points; it does not grant them unconditionally.

violations.quote: Wheel Plow allows you to plow two additional fields whenever you use Farmland or Cultivation
violations.rule: Wheel Plow’s text specifies it works only once per game and only when used with the first person you place in a round, not on every use of Farmland or Cultivation.

violations.quote: Alchemists Lab amplifies your building resource income with each improvement play
violations.rule: Alchemists Lab is an action space that gives resources when you use that space, not when you play improvements.

violations.quote: double plowing each turn
violations.rule: Wheel Plow lets you plow 2 additional fields (for a total of 3), not simply double the normal plow

violations.quote: triggering Cottar on each occupation
violations.rule: Cottar’s text: “Each time you play or build an improvement, you get …” — it does not trigger on playing Occupation cards

violations.quote: yielding wood which then triggers Cottar for extra clay or wood
violations.rule: Cottar only triggers on playing or building Improvements, not on gaining resources from other card effects

violations.quote: Cottar’s resource gains on occupation plays
violations.rule: Cottar triggers on playing or building Improvements, not on using Occupation spaces or playing Occupation cards

violations.quote: Brushwood Collector lets you replace reed costs with wood for room and improvement builds
violations.rule: Brushwood Collector: “Each time you renovate or build a room, you can replace the required 1 or 2 reed with a total of 1 wood.” It applies only to room builds, not improvements.

violations.quote: It works with Cottar since each stable built triggers bonus wood or clay
violations.rule: Cottar: “Each time you play or build an improvement, you get your choice of 1 wood or 1 clay.” It does not trigger when building stables.

violations.quote: "Wheel Plow secures your plow actions"
violations.rule: Wheel Plow is a one-time use: once per game when you use Farmland or Cultivation with your first person, you may plow 2 additional fields—it does not permanently secure all your plow actions.

violations.quote: "replacing reed costs with wood on improvements lets you trigger Cottar’s wood/clay payoff more often"
violations.rule: Farmyard Manure Collector triggers only when you renovate or build a room, not when you play or build an Improvement card; it does not replace reed costs on Improvements.

violations.quote: "each stable build (an improvement) triggers both Cottar and Feed Fence’s food payoff"
violations.rule: Building stables is not building an Improvement card; Cottar triggers only when you play or build an Improvement card, not when you build stables.

violations.quote: "Cottar can help supply wood/stone for room builds"
violations.rule: Cottar’s text: “Each time you play or build an Improvement, you get… wood or clay.” It does not trigger on building rooms, only on playing or building Improvement cards.

violations.quote: action spaces (Pasture, Family Growth, Grain Seeds) will be contested
violations.rule: There is no “Pasture” action space; pastures are farmyard structures, not a placement action

violations.quote: triggering Cottar’s improvement payoff each time you enlarge your house
violations.rule: Cottar triggers only when you play or build an Improvement card, not when you build rooms

violations.quote: Paper Maker converts Shoreforester-generated wood and Cottar-granted resources into food before each subsequent occupation, sustaining your action plan.
violations.rule: Paper Maker’s text: “Immediately before playing each occupation after this one, you can pay 1 wood total to get 1 food for each occupation you have in front of you.” It only converts wood, not arbitrary resources from Cottar.

violations.quote: Stable Yard doubles down on Feed Fence and helps shore up food when building stables
violations.rule: Stable Yard only gives food per remaining rounds when played and allows exchanging sheep + wild boar for cattle; it does not trigger on building stables.

violations.quote: Carpenter triggers room builds, which fire both Cottar and Shoreforester for wood/clay and wood
violations.rule: Cottar triggers on playing or building improvements (not rooms) and Shoreforester triggers on reeds placed on Reed Bank (not on room builds); Carpenter merely reduces room‐building costs.

violations.quote: it outperforms Corn Schnapps Distillery because it requires no recurring resource investment
violations.rule: Corn Schnapps Distillery requires paying 1 grain each round to place food tokens (a recurring resource cost).

violations.quote: providing family growth without room-building actions
violations.rule: Farm Hand grants a free stable (which provides room), but does not grant any Family Growth action or growth itself

violations.quote: Priest brings clay, reed, and stone when you build exactly two clay rooms
violations.rule: Priest grants 3 clay, 2 reed, 2 stone on play if you already live in a clay house with exactly 2 rooms, not when you build two clay rooms

violations.quote: one-off Feed Fence payoff
violations.rule: Feed Fence triggers each time you build stables; it is a repeatable effect, not a one-off

violations.quote: triggering Farm Hand to build a stable for just 1 food
violations.rule: Farm Hand’s card text makes the 1 Food cost apply only to playing the Occupation, not to building the stable; the stable is built as part of the card effect and carries no Food cost

violations.quote: and triggers Feed Fence for additional food and Cottar for a resource refund
violations.rule: Cottar triggers only when you play or build an Improvement; building a stable is not an Improvement and does not trigger Cottar

violations.quote: Synergizes with Cottar: each clay room built refunds wood or clay
violations.rule: Cottar triggers only on playing or building Improvements; building rooms (including clay rooms) is not an Improvement and does not trigger Cottar

violations.quote: Cottar to boost your stable‐build outputs
violations.rule: Cottar triggers only when you play or build an improvement card, not when you build stables (Minor Improvement text: “Each time you play or build an improvement, you get your choice of 1 wood or 1 clay…”).

violations.quote: turning each new improvement into a suite of resources
violations.rule: Alchemists Lab is an action space that grants resources only when you use that action; it does not trigger off playing or building improvements

violations.quote: shoring up resources without extra worker placement
violations.rule: Alchemists Lab is a shared action space and requires placing a Family member to use it

violations.quote: up to 18 bonus points over six harvests
violations.rule: Beer Table gives 2 bonus points per harvest, for a maximum of 6 × 2 = 12 bonus points

violations.quote: Alchemists Lab is the missing action hub that lets you play more minors
violations.rule: Alchemists Lab’s text gives you building resources but does not allow you to play Minor Improvements; you still need a proper Improvement action space to play them

violations.quote: letting you play more minors without spending scarce actions
violations.rule: Using Alchemists Lab grants resources only; it does not grant an action to play Minors or bypass the need for a Minor Improvement action

violations.quote: synergizes with Feed Fence and Special Food by ... rebuilding stables for food and VP
violations.rule: Feed Fence grants only Food when you build stables; building stables does not grant any Victory Points

violations.quote: rather than relying on an uncertain Fishing flip order
violations.rule: Mill Wheel triggers when you use Grain Utilization while the Fishing space is occupied; it does not depend on any “flip” order

violations.quote: popping ... Mud Wallower to fill pastures and stock boars
violations.rule: Mud Wallower places boar tokens on the card, not into pastures on your farm; it does not build or populate pastures directly

violations.quote: fills your biggest gap by converting idle wood accumulation spaces into both wood and food at harvest
violations.rule: Wood Harvester gives either 1 wood for each wood space with exactly 2 wood OR 1 food for each wood space with at least 3 wood; it does not give both for the same space

violations.quote: Synergizes with Shoreforester’s extra wood generation and Cottar’s improvement-triggered wood/clay
violations.rule: Wood Harvester triggers off wood on accumulation spaces, not wood in your supply; Shoreforester and Cottar give wood to your supply, so they do not increase wood on accumulation spaces for Wood Harvester to convert

violations.quote: Cottar and Paper Maker reward playing many improvements.
violations.rule: Paper Maker’s text triggers when playing Occupations, not Improvements—it rewards occupation plays, not minor improvements.

violations.quote: Grain-for-points cards (Beer Table, Ale-Benches, Market Crier) add some bonus scoring
violations.rule: Market Crier grants extra grain and a vegetable (and gives opponents grain); it does not grant Victory Points and is not a 'grain-for-points' card.

violations.quote: Leverages Pasture Master and Feed Fence to supply animals
violations.rule: Feed Fence grants food and alternate stable cost, it does not provide any animals.

violations.quote: granting 4+ extra food per trip
violations.rule: Stone Weir grants additional food of 4/3/2/1 depending on accumulation, never more than 4.

violations.quote: Lesson cards and Market Crier provide bonus points
violations.rule: Market Crier grants resources (grain and vegetable), it does not award any bonus points.

violations.quote: Several VP sources (Pasture Master, Tutor/Paper Maker)
violations.rule: Pasture Master has no printed VP and its effect grants food and animals on renovation, not victory points

violations.quote: this unique action gives up to 9 goods over four uses
violations.rule: Collector actually gives 6/7/8/9 goods on its 1st/2nd/3rd/4th use (total 30 goods), not a maximum of 9 across all uses

violations.quote: Plant Fertilizer immediately doubles your per-field yield without extra actions.
violations.rule: Plant Fertilizer only lets you add 1 good to each field that has exactly 1 good; it does not double yield on all fields.

violations.quote: Beats alternatives like Sundial since it grants tangible, repeatable benefit rather than limited free sow actions.
violations.rule: Thunderbolt’s effect is a one-time benefit when played and is not repeatable.

violations.quote: Several of the best minors (Renovation Company, Mantlepiece) are Stone House‐tagged but without a reliable early renovation you’ll struggle to hit their conditions.
violations.rule: Renovation Company’s prerequisite is “In Wooden House with Exactly 2 Rooms,” not a Stone House; it is not Stone House‐tagged.

violations.quote: It outclasses Grain Bag, which needs Bake improvements and plow actions you don’t yet have.
violations.rule: Grain Bag triggers on using the Grain Seeds action space and does not require any plow actions.

violations.quote: converting each breeding event into free plow actions
violations.rule: Dung Collector allows you to pay 1 Food to plow 1 field after a breeding event; it does not grant free plow actions

violations.quote: doubles grain on each newly sown field
violations.rule: Plant Fertilizer can only place an extra good on fields with exactly 1 good; it does not double grain on newly sown fields (which start with 3 grain)

violations.quote: relying on open Grain Seeds or sow space
violations.rule: There is no action space named “sow” — sowing is part of the Grain Utilization space

violations.quote: doubling goods on each plowed-and-sown field
violations.rule: Plant Fertilizer only allows placing 1 additional good on each field that has exactly 1 good; it does not double goods on plowed-and-sown fields

violations.quote: "Synergizes with your Ceilings by turning the wood you’ll receive on upcoming rounds into free clay and stone when you build rooms."
violations.rule: Renovation Preparer grants clay when you build wood rooms and grants stone when you build clay rooms; it does not convert wood directly into both clay and stone

violations.quote: "Helps supply stone for Artisan District and sheep for Breed Registry/Animal Husbandry Worker whenever opponents use accumulation spaces."
violations.rule: Buyer grants sheep, but Animal Husbandry Worker does not use sheep for any benefit

violations.quote: "provides an immediate sheep on play that feeds into Breed Registry and Animal Husbandry Worker."
violations.rule: Feed Pellets does give an immediate sheep, but Animal Husbandry Worker has no effect triggered by gaining or using sheep

violations.quote: No repeatable food sources beyond single-use Cultivator payouts
violations.rule: Roughcaster (Occupation): “Each time you build at least 1 clay room or renovate your house from clay to stone, you also get 3 food.” This is a repeatable food source beyond Cultivator.

violations.quote: No room building or family growth enablers drafted
violations.rule: Wood Saw (Minor Improvement): “Each time all other players have more people than you, you can take a ‘Build Rooms’ action.” This is a room-building enabler.

violations.quote: every new field tile yields grain and vegetables
violations.rule: Cultivator (Occupation): “For each new field tile you get, you also get 1 wood and 1 food.” It does not yield grain or vegetables.

violations.quote: without any resource cost
violations.rule: Changeover (Minor Improvement): “…you can discard that good and immediately take a ‘Sow’ action….” The Sow action still requires using seed from your supply, per sowing rules.

violations.quote: converting animals into repeated stable resources
violations.rule: Stable Cleaner does not convert animals into resources; it simply allows building stables without placing a person at a cost of 1 wood and 1 food each.

violations.quote: Works with Cultivator by converting plowed fields into clay
violations.rule: Field Clay gives clay equal to the number of planted fields you have when you play it; it does not convert plowed (empty) fields into clay.

violations.quote: only Veggie Lover and Feed Pellets provide limited food.
violations.rule: Feed Pellets does not provide food; it gives an animal or animal exchange, not food.

violations.quote: Task Artisan and Artisan District give some bonus points
violations.rule: Task Artisan grants wood and Minor Improvement actions, but does not provide any bonus points; only Artisan District grants bonus points.

violations.quote: Opponents snapped up Collier and Collector, indicating wood accumulation and minor improvement spaces will be contested.
violations.rule: Collier triggers on the Clay Pit and Hollow (clay accumulation spaces), not wood accumulation, and Collector is an Occupation that provides a personal action space, not a Minor Improvement space.

violations.quote: Plant Fertilizer doubles the yield on any field with a single good.
violations.rule: Card text: “In each field with exactly 1 good, you can immediately place 1 additional good of the same type.” It adds one good, not doubling yield.

violations.quote: Renovation Company (stone‐house support)
violations.rule: Renovation Company only upgrades a Wooden house to a Clay house (it grants 3 clay and a free Clay renovation), it does not support Stone house renovation.

violations.quote: granting a free occupation play and 2 food each time seeds are sown
violations.rule: Seed Researcher triggers only when both the Grain Seeds and Vegetable Seeds spaces are used in the same round, granting 2 food and one free Occupation play; it does not trigger on every single sow action.

violations.quote: scoring 1 point each time opponents sow
violations.rule: Publican only grants 1 point if you first give the sower 1 grain from your supply; it does not score automatically on every sow without paying that grain.

violations.quote: provides a midgame grain→food conversion if you sow fields
violations.rule: Beer Tap allows grain→food conversion only during the Harvest feeding phase (2/3/4 grain into 3/6/9 food), not immediately or upon sowing fields.

violations.quote: Provides free points whenever opponents use the Grain Seeds action
violations.rule: Publican triggers each time before another player takes an unconditional Sow action, not when they take the Grain Seeds action

violations.quote: Offers 2 food and a free occupation play on each seeds-refill
violations.rule: Seed Researcher triggers only when people return from both the Grain Seeds and Vegetable Seeds spaces in the same round, not on each individual seed-space refill

violations.quote: Provides 2 stone and 2 wood immediately to play bottom-row major improvements and trigger Task Artisan.
violations.rule: Task Artisan triggers only when you play the Task Artisan card and when a stone accumulation space appears on a round card; gaining or placing stone from Mayor Candidate does not trigger it.

violations.quote: Each Forest or Clay Pit play seeds a stone on the alternate space and grants an extra worker placement, triggering another wood + Minor Improvement action.
violations.rule: The extra worker placement from Inner Districts Director does not trigger Task Artisan; Task Artisan only triggers on playing itself and on stone‐accumulation spaces appearing, not on extra placements.

violations.quote: You’ve built strong wood accumulation via Ceilings and Private Forest and a fence engine with Animal Husbandry Worker/Stable Cleaner
violations.rule: Stable Cleaner grants a Build Stables action, not a Build Fences action; it does not provide any fence-building capability

violations.quote: instantly placing a field tile (triggering wood+food)
violations.rule: Patch Caregiver does not place a field tile on the farmyard when played; it only counts as a field for scoring purposes and does not trigger plow-related effects

violations.quote: fills the early food gap with repeat vegetable purchases and immediate grain
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker requires spending 2 food to buy 1 vegetable (net –1 food) each harvest; it does not fill a food gap

violations.quote: fills the missing ramp-up food and vegetable gap each harvest
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker does not provide food; it allows buying 1 vegetable for 2 food at each harvest (it consumes food rather than giving it)

violations.quote: It addresses your extra-action shortfall and reliably produces grain and wood each round.
violations.rule: Steam Plow grants extra Farmland actions (placing fields) but does not produce grain or wood; Farmland yields no resources when used.

violations.quote: yet no plow or growth enabler to start fields or add family members early
violations.rule: The Seed Almanac is present in the round-1 draft pool and is a plow enabler Minor Improvement.

violations.quote: No occupation or improvement provides recurring side‐effect actions yet
violations.rule: Master Renovator (in the same draft pool) grants two free Renovation actions at the end of rounds 7 and 9.

violations.quote: Education Bonus and Beer Keg can generate points
violations.rule: Education Bonus grants resources only—it does not grant bonus points; only Beer Keg can generate points.

violations.quote: Land Heir … ensuring you can afford stone rooms or major improvements when you renovate
violations.rule: Land Heir deposits wood and clay only; stone rooms and major improvements require stone (and reed for renovation), so Land Heir does not directly provide the needed stone.

violations.quote: Winter Caretaker covers harvest food
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker’s text gives you the ability at the end of each Harvest to buy exactly 1 vegetable for 2 Food—it does not provide Food during the Harvest.

violations.quote: Bonehead … will give 1 wood each time you play another occupation
violations.rule: Bonehead’s text grants you 1 wood after you play any card from your hand (including minors), not only occupations.

violations.quote: each veg you plant and harvest can be converted to food via its buy action
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker’s buy action converts 2 food into 1 vegetable, not vegetables into food.

violations.quote: Bonehead and Education Bonus reward every play
violations.rule: Education Bonus only triggers after you play your 1st/2nd/.../6th Occupation, not on every card play

violations.quote: Without a plow, you can’t exploit Melon Patch’s free field actions
violations.rule: Melon Patch’s card text grants you a plow action (outside the Work phase) when you harvest the last vegetable from it, so you do not need the Farmland space to plow that field.

violations.quote: Lesson and Occupation action spaces could get busy
violations.rule: There is only one action space, called “Lessons” (card text); “Occupation” is the old rulebook name and not a separate space in this app.

violations.quote: with only one Lesson card (Education Bonus)
violations.rule: Education Bonus is a Minor Improvement, not an Occupation (‘Lesson’) card; it does not count as a Lesson card.

violations.quote: Porter and Winter Caretaker provide occasional food
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker does not provide food; it grants 1 grain on play and allows buying vegetables for 2 food at each harvest, but gives no food.

violations.quote: The Renovation space in round 5 will be contested by bigger house strategies
violations.rule: The House Redevelopment (Renovation) space appears randomly in Stage 2 (rounds 5–7), not specifically in round 5.

violations.quote: No dedicated food engine beyond Winter Caretaker
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker grants 1 grain on play and offers buying 1 vegetable for 2 food at harvest; it does not produce food directly and is not a food‐generation engine

violations.quote: You have Melon Patch and Ed. Bonus for some bonus points
violations.rule: Education Bonus grants resources (grain/clay/reed/stone/vegetable/field) when playing occupations and has no scoring effect

violations.quote: adding reliable clay whenever you take clay
violations.rule: Clay Carrier lets you once per round buy 2 clay for 2 food on demand; it does not trigger when you take clay from an accumulation space

violations.quote: Winter Caretaker and Bonehead/Sleight of Hand conversion provide moderate food reserves
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker gives 1 grain on play and allows buying 1 vegetable for 2 food (a cost), while Bonehead and Sleight of Hand generate or convert building resources, not food

violations.quote: No plow cards or sow enablers in hand or drafted
violations.rule: The Melon Patch Minor Improvement allows you to plow 1 field when you harvest its last vegetable, and Garden Hoe gives rewards when sowing vegetables, so there are plow and sow enablers drafted

violations.quote: each occupation played (Bonehead, Winter Caretaker, Porter, new picks) nets immediate wood from Writing Boards
violations.rule: Writing Boards: “You immediately get 1 wood for each occupation you have in front of you.” This occurs only when you play the card, not on each subsequent occupation played.

violations.quote: Superior to Granary because it boosts your core engine every time you play an Occupation, not just on fixed rounds.
violations.rule: Writing Boards does not trigger for each occupation play. It only provides wood once, at the moment you play the card, not on later occupation plays.

violations.quote: Works with Melon Patch by doubling vegetable sow actions, boosting harvest yield;
violations.rule: Tinsmith Master lets you place exactly 1 additional crop per sow action, not double the usual yield.

violations.quote: scales with every new occupation play
violations.rule: Writing Boards grants a one-time wood bonus for occupations you have when you play it; it does not trigger on future occupation plays.

violations.quote: Your only food sources are intermittent (Winter Caretaker, Melon Patch) and won’t scale to a 4+ member family without baking or animal cooking.
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker gives 1 grain when played and allows you to buy vegetables (at the cost of food), but does not provide food itself.

violations.quote: Writing Boards ready to reward occupation plays
violations.rule: Writing Boards grants wood only once, on play, based on the number of occupations you already have; it does not trigger on occupation plays.

violations.quote: Winter Caretaker and Melon Patch give a baseline
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker provides grain on play and a vegetable‐purchase option, not food, and Melon Patch yields a plow action when you clear its vegetables, not food.

violations.quote: boosting vegetable output that Winter Caretaker can convert to food
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker’s card lets you spend food to acquire vegetables; it does not convert vegetables into food.

violations.quote: Works with Stock Protector: every time you enclose a new space building rooms or pastures, you get 2 stone to build more stone rooms for Half-Timbered House.
violations.rule: Trimmer triggers only when you enclose a pasture space by completing a fence; it does not trigger from building rooms.

violations.quote: Beats Potato Harvester because it fires every time you fence rather than only at harvest
violations.rule: Potato Harvester also has an immediate effect when played (gaining 3 food), not only a harvest-phase bonus.

violations.quote: No family-growth or room-building enablers drafted
violations.rule: Reader [Occupation]: “As soon as you have 6 occupations in front of you (including this one), this card provides room for one person.” (a room-building enabler is present)

violations.quote: Only Melon Patch’s one field-plow trigger and no dedicated plow cards
violations.rule: Steam Plow [Minor Improvement]: “Immediately after each returning home phase, you can pay 2 wood and 1 food to use the ‘Farmland’ action space without placing a person.” and Double-Turn Plow [Minor Improvement]: “When you play this card, you can immediately plow up to 2 fields.” (two plow cards are drafted)

violations.quote: Generates 1 grain each round you hold at least one sheep
violations.rule: Mineral Feeder [Minor Improvement]: “At the start of each round that does not end with a harvest, if you have at least 1 sheep in a pasture, you get 1 grain.” (does not trigger on harvest rounds)

violations.quote: synergizing with Winter Caretaker’s vegetable-for-food option
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker: “At the end of each harvest, you can buy exactly 1 vegetable for 2 food.” (It costs food to get a vegetable, not vice versa.)

violations.quote: Mineral Feeder provides at least 1 grain per round when you have sheep
violations.rule: Mineral Feeder: “At the start of each round that does not end with a harvest, if you have at least 1 sheep in a pasture, you get 1 grain.” (It does not trigger in harvest rounds.)

violations.quote: No passive action generators (Stone House, Traveling Players, Stable) secured
violations.rule: A renovated Stone House grants housing but no extra actions; stables increase animal capacity only, and neither “Stone House” nor stables grant actions.

violations.quote: No passive action generators (Stone House, Traveling Players, Stable) secured
violations.rule: Traveling Players is an accumulation space that yields 1 Food per round, not a passive action generator.

violations.quote: No passive action generators (Stone House, Traveling Players, Stable) secured
violations.rule: Stables do not provide or generate actions; they only double or increase animal capacity.

violations.quote: reward[s] playing cards, giving you a strong extra-actions backbone
violations.rule: Bonehead, Education Bonus, and Writing Boards each grant resources when triggered but none grant additional actions.

violations.quote: Playing Forest Owner triggers … Writing Boards for … wood
violations.rule: Writing Boards grants wood only when you play Writing Boards itself; it does not trigger on playing other cards.

violations.quote: As an occupation play, it triggers … Writing Boards
violations.rule: Writing Boards does not trigger on playing other occupations; its one-time effect occurs only when you play Writing Boards.

violations.quote: (1) It synergizes with every food action by converting food pickups into free wood, boosting both Day Laborer or Cooking Hearth plays.
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer only triggers when you get food from an action space; Cooking Hearth conversions do not use an action space and thus do not trigger Kindling Gatherer.

violations.quote: (1) Leverages your two starting rooms to net 3 wood instantly, fueling early room or fence building.
violations.rule: Baseboards gives 1 wood per room and an extra wood only if rooms > family members; with 2 rooms and 2 members you get 2 wood, not 3.

violations.quote: Forest Owner … directly fills your biggest gap in building resource supply without requiring extra actions or food.
violations.rule: Forest Owner is an action space that requires placing a Family member (and consumes an action) to gain wood, and you must pay the normal food cost to play the occupation.

violations.quote: It’s superior to Land Surveyor because it compounds on every occupation play in an undercontested space
violations.rule: Forest Owner triggers only when the Forest Owner card’s action space is used, not on every occupation play.

violations.quote: Den Builder directly creates a room
violations.rule: Den Builder does not place a new room tile; it provides room capacity for exactly one person (it ‘provides room for exactly one person’ rather than building a room).

violations.quote: Converts wood and stone into food at each round end
violations.rule: Sculpture Course triggers only at the end of rounds that do NOT end with a harvest; it cannot be used at every round end.

violations.quote: with Kindling Gatherer’s extra wood on food you get a compounding food＋wood loop
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only when you get food from an action space; it does not trigger on food gained from card effects at round end.

violations.quote: giving you 1 wood every time you gain food
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only when you get food from an action space, not any time you gain food

violations.quote: giving wood equal to your rooms (plus one extra)
violations.rule: Baseboards gives 1 wood per room immediately, and the extra wood only if you have more rooms than people; it is not unconditional

violations.quote: provides scalable wood every turn rather than a one-time grain+veg gain
violations.rule: Baseboards grants wood only once on play, it does not provide recurring wood each turn

violations.quote: free wood and extra person before fencing
violations.rule: Stock Protector grants the extra person after the Fencing action, not before

violations.quote: which works seamlessly with Kindling Gatherer to convert those food gains into wood
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only on food gained from an action space, and Food Basket gives grain and vegetables (not food), so it does not trigger on Food Basket’s resources

violations.quote: you have Kindling Gatherer for incidental food boosts
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer gives 1 wood when you get food from an action space—it does not grant food.

violations.quote: indirectly triggering Kindling Gatherer each time you collect food from grain fields
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer only triggers on food from an action space; harvesting grain from fields gives grain, not food, and is not an action space.

violations.quote: Lynchet…supports Kindling Gatherer’s wood engine
violations.rule: Lynchet provides food during the harvest phase, which does not count as getting food from an action space and therefore does not trigger Kindling Gatherer.

violations.quote: Lynchet and Scythe Worker yield food from fields
violations.rule: Scythe Worker gives 1 additional GRAIN from each grain field, not FOOD

violations.quote: Consultant immediately yields grain for sowing/harvest synergy with Scythe Worker and Lynchet, plus clay and reed to build rooms and feed with Baseboards
violations.rule: In a 4-player game Consultant grants 2 SHEEP only (no grain, clay or reed)

violations.quote: Sowing Master directly complements your field focus—each sow action gives 2 food, boosting your harvest-based engine and triggering Kindling Gatherer’s wood bonus
violations.rule: The 2 Food from Sowing Master is a card effect, not food from an action space, so Kindling Gatherer does not trigger

violations.quote: It triggers Kindling Gatherer’s wood bonus on food rounds
violations.rule: Muddy Waters yields food at the start of rounds, not from an action space, so Kindling Gatherer does not trigger

violations.quote: Chicken Coop delivers 1 food each round for eight rounds, underpinning your engine and triggering Kindling Gatherer for extra wood
violations.rule: Chicken Coop grants food at the start of rounds, not from an action space, so Kindling Gatherer does not trigger

violations.quote: Sowing Master or Pan Baker, which don’t address the immediate building resource crunch.
violations.rule: Pan Baker: each time you use the Grain Utilization action space, you also get 2 clay and 1 wood, so it does provide building resources.

violations.quote: turning each improvement play into 3 food (which then generates 3 wood)
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers once per action-space event, not once per food, so 3 food from Small Trader yields only 1 wood, not 3.

violations.quote: generating food each harvest and triggering Kindling Gatherer’s wood bonus
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only when you get food from an action space, not from harvest-phase effects like Lynchet.

violations.quote: whereas Sculpture Course depends on paying grain and running wood-or-stone conversions
violations.rule: Sculpture Course costs wood or stone, never grain.

violations.quote: no need to breed boars or fence fields
violations.rule: Mud Patch holds wild boars on unplanted field tiles and does not require fenced pastures.

violations.quote: works every round
violations.rule: Sculpture Course activates only at the end of rounds that do not end with a harvest, not literally every round.

violations.quote: "Lynchet and Scythe Worker provide solid field scoring; additional scoring depends on room builds"
violations.rule: Lynchet grants food per adjacent harvested field and Scythe Worker grants extra grain per grain field; neither card grants Victory Points or direct scoring bonuses.

violations.quote: you’ll miss out on the vital 2 food per new person actions
violations.rule: Family Growth and related growth actions do not grant any Food; a new family member action gives no Food (rules §2 Phase 2 and §4 Family growth).

violations.quote: Lynchet and Scythe Worker provide harvest food
violations.rule: Scythe Worker grants additional Grain (not Food) during the Field phase; only Lynchet grants Food in harvest (card text).

violations.quote: for extra wood-to-food conversions
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer grants extra Wood when you get Food from an action space; there is no Wood-to-Food conversion (rules §2 Phase 2 and card text).

violations.quote: Scholar and Overachiever will unlock additional plays but require renovation to activate fully
violations.rule: Overachiever’s ability triggers on using the Wish for Children action and does not require any Renovation or house type; only Scholar requires a Stone house (card texts).

violations.quote: you’ve snapped Baseboards and Muddy Waters for resource drips
violations.rule: Baseboards gives a one-time wood bonus on play (and a conditional one-time bonus), not a recurring drip on future rounds

violations.quote: Scythe Worker yields extra grain; Baker gives you a Bake Bread action each harvest to turn that grain into food.
violations.rule: Baker grants Bake Bread actions but converting grain to food also requires a Baking Improvement (e.g. Fireplace or Cooking Hearth); the action alone does not automatically bake grain

violations.quote: letting you chain multiple room builds and trigger Baseboards’ wood payout infinitely
violations.rule: Baseboards only pays out immediately when played (you get wood based on existing rooms once); it has no ongoing trigger and cannot be retriggered by building rooms

violations.quote: Elder ensures you play one occupation free each round
violations.rule: Elder has no ongoing effect; it only lets you play itself at the start of round 1 and does not grant free occupation plays in subsequent rounds

violations.quote: Muddy Waters and Lynchet produce scalable food each harvest, reinforced by Kindling Gatherer’s wood conversion.
violations.rule: Muddy Waters triggers at the start of specified rounds (even-numbered), not in the Harvest phase; it does not produce food each harvest.

violations.quote: pairing with Hedge Keeper you can acquire sheep/boar at bargain rates whenever others build fences
violations.rule: Hedge Keeper reduces the wood cost when you build fences; it does not affect Cattle Buyer’s food cost or trigger, which only activates when other players build fences

violations.quote: Zero plow or sow enablers—fields can’t be reliably sown or reset
violations.rule: Changeover is a sow enabler: “At any time, if a field contains exactly 1 good as a result of a harvest, you can discard that good and immediately take a ‘Sow’ action limited to that field.”

violations.quote: …giving you the stone you’ll need for a future renovation or rooms
violations.rule: Building rooms costs only Wood and Reed (or Clay/Reed or Stone/Reed for higher‐level houses) and does not require Stone.

violations.quote: Converts every farmyard expansion into clay (and optional food), feeding Kindling Gatherer and supporting room/stable builds.
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only when you get food from an action space; the food from Potter's Yard’s card effect is not from an action space and thus does not trigger Kindling Gatherer.

violations.quote: harvest any planted fields in the harvest phase
violations.rule: Scythe lets you harvest exactly one of your fields each harvest, not multiple fields

violations.quote: with Lynchet, Scythe Worker, Muddy Waters and Changeover amplifying each field tile for food and points
violations.rule: Muddy Waters and Changeover do not interact with harvested fields and neither Muddy Waters nor Changeover grant per-field food or points; Lynchet only grants food, not points, and Scythe Worker grants extra grain, not points

violations.quote: Pan Baker leverage your planned sow actions to generate food and resources
violations.rule: Pan Baker grants 2 clay and 1 wood when using the Grain Utilization space, but does not grant any food

violations.quote: Opponents have taken Swagman, signaling Grain Utilization will be contested
violations.rule: Swagman affects the Farm Expansion and Grain Seeds spaces, not the Grain Utilization (Sow and/or Bake bread) space

violations.quote: Ash Trees sets up a free-fence engine that sidelines fence actions
violations.rule: Ash Trees gives free fences by covering the wood cost, but it does not remove the requirement to take the Fencing action (or another fence-building action) to place fences.

violations.quote: Enhances every use of the Farmland/Cultivation action space by adding a free plow
violations.rule: Plow Hero lets you plow 1 additional field for 1 Food—it is not free.

violations.quote: Awards 1 food, 1 grain, 1 vegetable each time your #occupations played equals harvests completed
violations.rule: Harvest House triggers only once on play if at that moment your completed harvests equal occupations played; it does not trigger repeatedly

violations.quote: Ash Trees… makes all future fence-building cost-free
violations.rule: Ash Trees places up to 5 fences on the card that you may use without cost; it does not waive the cost of all fences indefinitely

violations.quote: There’s also no plow or sow synergy in your draft so far, making field work less efficient
violations.rule: You have Plow Hero in hand, which provides plow synergy when using Farmland or Cultivation

violations.quote: Chimney Sweep and upcoming Plowman can generate actions
violations.rule: Chimney Sweep’s card text grants no actions; it only reduces the cost to renovate to stone and gives a scoring bonus. Only Plowman grants free plow actions.

violations.quote: giving automatic fields each round
violations.rule: Plowman grants free plow actions on exactly three specified future rounds, not on every round.

violations.quote: Canvas Sack converts grain into vegetables or wood on demand
violations.rule: Canvas Sack requires paying grain to get a vegetable or paying reed to get wood; it does not convert grain into wood.

violations.quote: Chimney Sweep makes renovation cheaper so you can build a stable early
violations.rule: Chimney Sweep only reduces the cost to renovate your house to stone; it does not affect building stables.

violations.quote: Forest Owner is a complementary pick that enhances wood income every round
violations.rule: Forest Owner is an action space for all players and only grants wood when a player places a family member there, not automatically every round

violations.quote: Plowman secures three future plow actions with harvest-time food
violations.rule: Plowman triggers at the start of rounds 4, 7, and 10, allowing you to plow a field and gain 1 food at the start of those rounds—not at harvest time.

violations.quote: fills your building resource gap with guaranteed wood each round
violations.rule: Drudgery Reeve gives wood only once when played (based on rounds remaining), not each round.

violations.quote: rewards a full farm once you renovate to stone and fill all categories
violations.rule: Lord of the Manor grants bonus points for each scoring category in which you hit the top band at scoring; it does not require renovating to stone.

violations.quote: "No food engine or accumulation in drafted cards"
violations.rule: Claypipe and Churchyard both generate food each round, so there are food‐engine/accumulation cards in the drafted pool

violations.quote: "No generated‐action cards yet"
violations.rule: Chief Forester grants an extra Sow action (and Ravenous Hunger also grants an extra placement), so generated‐action cards are present

violations.quote: "No plow or sow enablers drafted"
violations.rule: Ox Goad lets you pay food to plow a field and Chief Forester grants a Sow action, so plow and sow enablers are indeed drafted

violations.quote: The two minors so far (Harvest House, Canvas Sack) reward occupation plays
violations.rule: Canvas Sack has a prerequisite 'needs No Occupations' and does not reward occupation plays

violations.quote: every Cattle Market action gives you grain+food
violations.rule: Hoof Caregiver triggers once on play (adds cattle then gives grain+food for each cattle), not each time you use Cattle Market

violations.quote: Ox Goad’s free plow
violations.rule: Ox Goad lets you pay 2 Food to plow 1 field; it is not a free plow

violations.quote: Lord of the Manor and Harvest House provide solid bonus scoring
violations.rule: Harvest House grants 2 printed VP and gives resources on play but does not confer any bonus points at game end

violations.quote: Drops one food on each of the next four rounds plus one stone on the fifth, guaranteeing both food and a critical stone supply for Chimney Sweep’s early renovation
violations.rule: Club House places its 1 stone on the fifth upcoming round space—which falls after Stage 2’s Renovation (rounds 5–7)—so it cannot supply stone for early renovation

violations.quote: aligning with your renovation timing
violations.rule: The timing of Club House’s food and stone placements does not match the rounds when Renovation actions are available (Stage 2 or Stage 6)

violations.quote: "plow": "No plow equipment or dedicated sow/seeding support drafted"
violations.rule: The draft state includes Plow Hero and Mountain Plowman, both of which provide plow support (extra field plowing and sheep per plowed field)

violations.quote: Only Priest supports small-house growth; no additional growth enablers
violations.rule: Priest’s text grants resources when played but does not grant any Family Growth; other cards and the normal growth spaces provide growth.

violations.quote: Mountain Plowman rewards every plow action you’ll take while you sow or bake
violations.rule: Mountain Plowman triggers only when you plow fields (Farmland or Cultivation), not when you sow or bake bread; bake bread does not plow fields.

violations.quote: Clay Firer, which demands a stone-house pivot
violations.rule: Clay Firer allows clay→stone conversion at any time without needing to live in a stone house or pivot your house type.

violations.quote: Round 5 renovation
violations.rule: House Redevelopment appears on a random round within Stage 2 (rounds 5–7), not specifically in round 5

violations.quote: every time you build a room or later a major improvement, you bank food on upcoming rounds, smoothing your midgame
violations.rule: Farm Building triggers only when you build a major improvement, not when you build rooms

violations.quote: Brick Hammer offers occasional stone when you build your clay/stone rooms
violations.rule: Brick Hammer triggers when you build an improvement costing at least 2 clay; it does not trigger on building rooms

violations.quote: spaces like Day Laborer and Empty Stable may be contested
violations.rule: There is no 'Empty Stable' action space in Agricola; stables are built via Farm Expansion or card effects, but there is no main-board 'Empty Stable' placement spot.

violations.quote: Without growth or plow coverage, we’ll struggle to build the rooms or fields needed to trigger Priest or Town Hall
violations.rule: Priest triggers on having exactly two rooms in a clay house (no fields required), and Town Hall triggers on living in a clay or stone house (fields are irrelevant).

violations.quote: Town Hall provides 1 food each harvest for a clay or stone house
violations.rule: Town Hall grants 1 food for a clay house and 2 food for a stone house each harvest, not just 1 food for both.

violations.quote: lack steady resource generation—especially wood—for renovation and room building
violations.rule: Renovation (to clay or stone) requires clay/stone and reed, never wood

violations.quote: No generated-action occupations or improvements to supplement worker placements
violations.rule: Tea Time grants an extra worker placement by returning your person on Grain Utilization for a second placement

violations.quote: No cards to add family members or expanded actions
violations.rule: Tea Time provides an expanded action (a second placement) rather than no expanded actions

violations.quote: Pairs with Chimney Sweep’s cheap renovation by giving you a reliable wood source for both rooms and stone upgrade
violations.rule: Stone renovation uses stone and reed (not wood), and Chimney Sweep reduces stone cost only; wood income does not help with stone upgrade

violations.quote: "point_ceiling": "Lord of the Manor and Harvest House give endgame bonus potential but no major improvements"
violations.rule: Harvest House only provides an immediate resource bonus when played and 2 printed VP; it has no end‐of‐game bonus‐point effect.

violations.quote: "food": "No scalable food engine; reliant on Winter Caretaker and Harvest House get food only sporadically"
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker grants grain and the option to buy a vegetable for 2 food—it does not itself provide food, so it is not a source of food.

violations.quote: "It’s better than Forest Inn since it’s always available"
violations.rule: Paper Knife is a Minor Improvement that must be played via an improvement action space and only triggers once on play; it is not an always‐available action.

violations.quote: a suite of resource-generating minors (Canvas Sack, Muddy Waters, Ox Goad)
violations.rule: Ox Goad does not generate resources; it costs 2 Food to plow a field and produces no goods

violations.quote: Muddy Waters, Winter Caretaker, Ox Goad and Harvest House give periodic food
violations.rule: Winter Caretaker does not produce Food; it lets you spend Food to buy Vegetables, and Harvest House is a one-time gain on play, not a recurring effect

violations.quote: Muddy Waters, Winter Caretaker, Ox Goad and Harvest House give periodic food
violations.rule: Harvest House’s effect triggers only once on play for 1 Food/1 Grain/1 Vegetable, not each round

violations.quote: No cards yet to expand your family or generate extra actions
violations.rule: Chief Forester grants an extra “Sow” action each time you use a wood accumulation space, so the draft does include an extra-action card

violations.quote: Freemason and Muddy Waters generate clay each round
violations.rule: Muddy Waters places Clay only on alternating even-numbered rounds, not each round

violations.quote: Priest gives the 1 stone and 1 reed needed to play Churchyard
violations.rule: Priest actually grants 3 Clay, 2 Reed, and 2 Stone when played, not 1 Stone and 1 Reed

violations.quote: Rewards the fields you’ll be sowing with future Grain or Vegetable Seeds actions
violations.rule: Lynchet triggers in the field phase of each harvest for harvested field tiles adjacent to your house; it does not interact with Grain Seeds or Vegetable Seeds actions

violations.quote: occupations that accelerate animal acquisition (Haydryer, Ranch Provost)
violations.rule: Ranch Provost does not accelerate animal acquisition; it grants wood and end-game bonus points but has no effect on animals.

violations.quote: It guarantees a free Growth action at your next harvest
violations.rule: Bed in the Grain Field grants a Family Growth action at the start of the next harvest only if you have room for the newborn (it is not unconditional)

violations.quote: Provides two extra worker-placements without costing food
violations.rule: Bed in the Grain Field gives exactly one extra Family Growth action (one placement), not two

violations.quote: Clay Deliveryman turns occupation plays into clay drops every round
violations.rule: Clay Deliveryman actually places 1 clay on each remaining round space for rounds 6–14 and gives that clay at the start of those rounds; it does not trigger on occupation plays.

violations.quote: Bed in the Grain Field works hand-in-hand with Bookshelf’s free food to guarantee a Family Growth action at your next harvest
violations.rule: Bed in the Grain Field only grants a Family Growth action at the next harvest if you have room for the newborn; it is not an unconditional guarantee.

violations.quote: Carpenter’s Axe grants free stable builds after wood trips
violations.rule: Carpenter’s Axe actually allows you to build 1 stable for 1 wood after using a wood accumulation space—it is not free

violations.quote: Drudgery Reeve provides 1–4 wood each round
violations.rule: Drudgery Reeve grants you 1–4 wood immediately when you play it (depending on rounds remaining), not each round

violations.quote: which you can then immediately convert into stables via Carpenter’s Axe
violations.rule: Carpenter’s Axe only triggers after using a wood accumulation space (Forest, Grove, Copse), not after an occupation’s wood generation like Drudgery Reeve

violations.quote: converts sheep, boar, cattle, vegetables, and grain into food on demand
violations.rule: Earth Oven converts grain only when you take a Bake Bread action – grain conversion is not an 'at any time' effect

violations.quote: Converts sheep, boar, cattle (breeding output from Champion Breeder and Haydryer) into food
violations.rule: Champion Breeder does not produce any animals; it only awards bonus points when animals breed, while Haydryer adds cattle—Champion Breeder has no effect on animal production

violations.quote: Consultant instantly provides 2 sheep and 3 clay (for early stabling)
violations.rule: Consultant in a 4-player game only provides 2 sheep; it does not also grant 3 clay

violations.quote: Provides a free plow every round after renovation
violations.rule: Plow Driver requires paying 1 food to plow a field each round once you live in a stone house; it is not a free plow

violations.quote: Champion Breeder and Haydryer drive cattle/animal accumulation
violations.rule: Champion Breeder grants bonus points for placing newborn animals during breeding but does not generate or increase animal accumulation; it only scores points.

violations.quote: Champion Breeder and cooking conversions give moderate bonus points
violations.rule: Cooking improvements and conversion effects (e.g. Fireplace, Cooking Hearth, Earth Oven) convert resources to food, not points; they have printed VP but do not grant bonus points for conversions

violations.quote: immediately convert via Earth Oven into 2 additional food
violations.rule: Earth Oven does not convert wood; it converts only vegetables, sheep, wild boar, cattle, or grain

violations.quote: while triggering Stable Tree’s wood drops
violations.rule: Stable Tree triggers only when you build stables, not when you convert resources via Earth Oven

violations.quote: triggering Carpenter’s Axe
violations.rule: Carpenter’s Axe triggers only after using a wood accumulation space with ≥7 wood, not from building stables via Pole Barns

violations.quote: triggering Stable Tree three times to seed wood on upcoming rounds
violations.rule: Stable Tree triggers once per turn when you build one or more stables, not once per stable built

violations.quote: robust food backup via Earth Oven and Haydryer
violations.rule: Haydryer doesn’t provide food directly; it lets you buy a cattle for food before each harvest (costing food) and only yields meat to be cooked later, not immediate food

violations.quote: Your only Lesson support (Bookshelf, Night-School Student) has not coalesced into a full Lesson engine
violations.rule: The Bookshelf improvement triggers on playing an Occupation (giving 3 food), and does not interact with the Lessons action space at all.

violations.quote: animal scoring (Champion Breeder, Misanthropy)
violations.rule: Misanthropy scores bonus points based on the number of Family members (people), not animals

violations.quote: (1) Compliments Drudgery Reeve and Carpenter's Axe by turning wood accumulation trips into incremental food, helping bridge feeding gaps.
violations.rule: Drudgery Reeve grants wood at the start of rounds, not from using a wood accumulation space, so Woodcraft does not trigger on Reeve’s wood

violations.quote: Build Wood actions
violations.rule: There is no action space called “Build Wood”; wood is gained from accumulation spaces (Forest, Grove, Copse) rather than a single “Build Wood” action

violations.quote: Only Earth Oven and Bookshelf supply food; no ongoing food engine
violations.rule: Multiple drafted cards provide food (e.g., Schnapps Distiller, Ebonist, Bellfounder, etc.), so food is not only from Earth Oven and Bookshelf

violations.quote: Thresher ensures you always have grain to feed into Earth Oven and to sow fields like Beanfield
violations.rule: Beanfield is a field that can only grow vegetables and requires vegetables to sow; Thresher only provides grain, so it cannot be used to sow Beanfield

violations.quote: Woodcraft grants 1 food each time you gather wood, synergizing with Drudgery Reeve’s repeated wood payouts
violations.rule: Woodcraft triggers only when using a wood accumulation space, not when receiving wood from Drudgery Reeve’s occupation effect

violations.quote: Woodcraft grants 1 food each time you gather wood, synergizing with Stable Tree’s wood generation
violations.rule: Woodcraft triggers only from using wood accumulation spaces, not from wood gained via Stable Tree’s round payouts

violations.quote: Canvas Sack and Vegetable Vendor provide occasional bonus actions
violations.rule: Canvas Sack text grants only immediate resources on play (1 vegetable/4 wood); it does not provide any bonus actions

violations.quote: Hewer turns lightly‐used clay spaces into dependable stone+food each round
violations.rule: Hewer’s text: “From round 3 on… at the end of each work phase in which all clay accumulation spaces are unoccupied, you get 1 stone and 1 food.” It does not trigger before round 3.

violations.quote: No reliable food source beyond Canvas Sack conversions
violations.rule: Canvas Sack does not provide food; it grants 1 vegetable or 4 wood when played, not food.

violations.quote: Wood Barterer pairs with Canvas Sack by generating wood or reed before any Build Rooms/Build Fences action, ensuring you can trigger the Canvas Sack payout
violations.rule: Wood Barterer’s effect triggers only before Build Rooms or Build Fences actions and does not apply to playing a Minor Improvement like Canvas Sack, so it cannot help pay for that card.

violations.quote: No cards yet that grant passive or side-effect actions
violations.rule: Vegetable Vendor and Wood Barterer both grant passive side-effect effects (Vegetable Vendor gives extra Vegetable or Improvement actions when using certain spaces; Wood Barterer gives wood or reed exchanges before certain spaces).

violations.quote: No high-VP minors drafted and only one bonus point occupation
