violations.rule: Neither drafted Occupation (Vegetable Vendor, Wood Barterer) grants bonus points, and no Minor Improvements have been drafted, so there are zero bonus-point occupations.

violations.quote: Synergizes with Canvas Sack by converting wood into reed so you can pay reed for Canvas Sack’s 4 wood bonus
violations.rule: Wood Barterer’s ability to exchange wood for reed only triggers “before you use an action space with a Build Fences or Build Rooms action.” Playing a Minor Improvement (Canvas Sack) is done on a Minor Improvement action space, not Build Rooms/Fences, so Wood Barterer cannot generate reed for that purpose.

violations.quote: supported by food holdover from Canvas Sack and Fodder Beets
violations.rule: Canvas Sack gives an immediate 1 vegetable or 4 wood when played and does not place food on future rounds—only Fodder Beets does.

violations.quote: Vegetable Vendor and future improvements yield scoring but no dedicated bonus-point cards yet
violations.rule: Vegetable Vendor grants extra vegetables or actions, not points—it has no scoring effect.

violations.quote: No plow improvements drafted, so fields and sowing are unavailable
violations.rule: Farmland (Plow 1 Field) and Grain Utilization (Sow) actions are always available in the game; you do not need any Minor Improvement to plow or sow.

violations.quote: Without Handplow, you’ll miss fields and lose Vegetable Vendor value
violations.rule: Fields can be plowed via the standard Farmland action without Handplow; you do not need Handplow to access fields.

violations.quote: Food is moderately addressed with Fodder Beets and Canvas Sack
violations.rule: Canvas Sack gives 1 vegetable or 4 wood when played, not any Food

violations.quote: growth is only backed by a single room-discount card
violations.rule: No card in the pool grants a discount on building rooms; Wood Barterer gives wood or lets you exchange wood for reed, but does not reduce room costs

violations.quote: feeds into Storeroom and Vegetable Vendor triggers
violations.rule: Storeroom scores pairs of grain + vegetable and Vegetable Vendor triggers on using Vegetable Seeds or Major Improvement spaces; neither cares about sheep from Horse-Drawn Boat

violations.quote: Seatmate guarantees you access to the Round 13 minor‐improvement action space, crucial for playing your final Storeroom or other minors even if neighbors block.
violations.rule: Seatmate lets you use the action space on round space 13 even if it's occupied, but that space is whatever Round-13 card happens to be, not the Minor Improvement space (which appears in an earlier round).

violations.quote: (1) Handplow gives you free plow actions and fields on two critical rounds
violations.rule: Handplow’s text only places one field tile on a single future round space and grants one plow at the start of that round; it does not provide two plow actions or fields

violations.quote: Fodder Beets and Tea House supply abundant food through every round
violations.rule: Fodder Beets places 1 food only on remaining odd‐numbered round spaces, not every round; Tea House gives at most 1 food per round when you skip placing your second person, not a consistent ‘abundant’ food each round

violations.quote: Tree Farm Joiner: "(1) Grants a one-time extra worker placement in a critical later round to relieve your growth and action crunch."
violations.rule: Telegram marks one future round per fence in your supply and gives an extra placement in each of those rounds, not just one

violations.quote: "Requires only 2 food—covered by Fodder Beets and Tea House—without depending on contested action spaces."
violations.rule: Telegram also has a prerequisite of at least 1 fence in your supply, not just a 2 Food cost

violations.quote: "No room-building/enabled growth cards beyond Wood Barterer"
violations.rule: Wood Barterer does not grant any room-building or Family Growth actions; it only provides resource bonuses before Build Rooms or Build Fences actions

violations.quote: Vegetable Vendor and Tutor yield some extra actions
violations.rule: Tutor does not yield any extra actions; its text gives only scoring bonus points, not actions.

violations.quote: Turns Fishing trips into Minor Improvement actions
violations.rule: Angler grants a “Major or Minor Improvement” action after Fishing, not exclusively a Minor Improvement action.

violations.quote: Stable actions
violations.rule: There is no “Stable” action space in Agricola; building stables is part of the “Farm Expansion” (Build Room(s) and/or Build Stable(s)) action space, and no separate Stable space exists

violations.quote: No cards currently generate ongoing actions aside from occupying Improvement spaces
violations.rule: Several cards (e.g. Tree Farm Joiner, Vegetable Vendor) explicitly grant additional actions (Minor or Major/Minor Improvement actions) outside of placing on action spaces, so card-granted actions do exist

violations.quote: providing clay, stone, reed or wood whenever you choose
violations.rule: Entrepreneur’s text lets you gain 1 building resource only at the start of each round when you move or discard food on the card, not at any time of your choosing

violations.quote: Opponents' picks of Comb and Cutter and Hewer signal Day Laborer and wood contention
violations.rule: Hewer triggers from round 3 on if clay accumulation spaces are unoccupied and gives 1 stone and 1 food; it has nothing to do with wood contention

violations.quote: Tutor, Tree Farm Joiner, and Tea House provide some side-actions
violations.rule: Tutor has no action ability; it only grants scoring points during final scoring

violations.quote: Immediately renovates your two clay rooms to stone for +4 VP
violations.rule: Established Person performs one renovation step (Wooden→Clay) without cost, not directly to Stone; two Clay rooms score only +2 VP in scoring, not +4

violations.quote: Combines perfectly with Tree Farm Joiner wood drops—feed this card wood to gain scarce clay, reed, or stone each round
violations.rule: Entrepreneur requires moving or discarding Food on the card, not Wood, to trigger its effect

violations.quote: Multiple round-space food engines (Fodder Beets, Wholesale Market, Tea House) give ample food for late-game harvests
violations.rule: Tea House does not place food on round spaces; it grants 1 food by skipping your second placement once per round, not a round-space engine

violations.quote: Entrepreneur generates one new building resource each round ... smoothing costs without costing food
violations.rule: Entrepreneur requires you to move or discard 1 food each round to gain a building resource, so it does cost food

violations.quote: Tutor and Vegetable Vendor grant bonus actions
violations.rule: Tutor grants bonus points during scoring, not actions

violations.quote: Tea House and Working Gloves give minor action relief
violations.rule: Working Gloves does not provide any extra action or action‐placement relief; it grants a discount on Food cost for playing Occupations

violations.quote: Multiple MIs (Fodder Beets, Wholesale Market, Tea House, Canvas Sack) plus potential Lesson feeding ease harvest feeding.
violations.rule: Canvas Sack gives vegetables or wood when played, not food.

violations.quote: It also outpaces the next-best Plowman by offering immediate resources and VP potential rather than future plow scheduling.
violations.rule: Occupations never have printed VP; Shed Builder grants resources when you build stables but does not grant any VP.

violations.quote: Wares Salesman (rank 123) is a high-play-rate complementary pick that will gain you wood and reed whenever you or opponents turn building resources into food (e.g. Beer Stall or Schnapps Distillery).
violations.rule: Wares Salesman triggers only when a card turns building resources (wood, clay, or reed) into food. Beer Stall and Schnapps Distillery convert grain and vegetables, which are crops, not building resources, so they do not trigger Wares Salesman.

violations.quote: "Loom and Beer Stall provide VP sources"
violations.rule: Beer Stall does not provide any printed victory points; only Loom has printed VP

violations.quote: Provides three free field placements on rounds 5–7
violations.rule: Plowman places field tiles on rounds current+4, +7, and +10 (so rounds 5, 8, and 11 when played in round 1) and each plow costs 1 food; it does not give free fields on rounds 5–7.

violations.quote: Prophet gives you a free Renovation and Build Fences action on play, directly enabling you to fence new stables without spending your action or resources
violations.rule: Card text: 'When you play this card, immediately take a “Renovation” action. Afterward, you can take a “Build Fences” action. (Both actions require their usual cost.)'—the actions still require resources

violations.quote: Shepherd’s Whistle is your third Stable-tag card, generating a sheep in each empty unfenced stable at breeding
violations.rule: Card text: 'At the start of the breeding phase of each harvest, if you have at least 1 unfenced stable without animal, you get 1 sheep.'—it grants only one sheep total, not one per stable

violations.quote: Beer Stall by allowing you to maintain empty fenced stables for grain-to-food conversions
violations.rule: Card text: 'In the feeding phase of each harvest, for each empty unfenced stable you have, you can exchange 1 grain for 5 food.'—it requires unfenced stables, not fenced

violations.quote: (3) More reliable than Pickler because it doesn’t depend on flip-order wood accumulation or contested vegetables.
violations.rule: Pickler’s wood gain is immediate based on rounds remaining and does not depend on using wood accumulation spaces; it grants wood on play according to rounds left.

violations.quote: After any wood accumulation you can build an extra stable for 1 wood
violations.rule: Carpenter's Axe requires that you have at least 7 wood in your supply after using a wood accumulation space before you may build a stable for 1 wood

violations.quote: (1) Works with Carpenter’s Axe by converting Reed Bank placements into wood for additional stables.
violations.rule: Carpenter’s Axe triggers only after using a wood accumulation space (Forest/Grove/Copse), not when gaining wood from Shoreforester on a Reed Bank placement. Shoreforester’s wood gain does not activate Carpenter’s Axe.

violations.quote: …and that grain also supports Beer Stall or Shepherd’s Whistle.
violations.rule: Shepherd’s Whistle triggers at the start of the breeding phase to give a sheep and has nothing to do with grain; grain cannot be spent or used to support Shepherd’s Whistle.

violations.quote: Beer Stall and Shepherd’s Whistle provide grain-to-food conversion but no scalable late-game food engine.
violations.rule: Shepherd’s Whistle grants a sheep at the start of the breeding phase if you have an empty unfenced stable; it does not convert grain to food.

violations.quote: Synergizes with Carpenter’s Axe and wood accumulation from stable rebuilds
violations.rule: There is no rule or card that grants "wood accumulation from stable rebuilds"; building or "rebuilding" stables does not yield wood.

violations.quote: focusing on generating grain/veg via Shed Builder and Beer Stall
violations.rule: Beer Stall does not generate grain or vegetables; it consumes grain to produce food (Beer Stall: In the feeding phase of each harvest, for each empty unfenced stable you have, you can exchange 1 grain for 5 food).

violations.quote: Pairs with your Pipe Smoker and Plow Maker to guarantee grain fields
violations.rule: The Plowman occupation places empty field tiles on specified rounds; it does not sow grain or guarantee fields with grain on them.

violations.quote: Plow synergies from Plowman and Plow Maker give you fields and grain to fuel that Stable engine.
violations.rule: Plowman and Plow Maker grant additional fields (plowing actions) but do not directly give any grain.

violations.quote: rendering three free field plows across the game
violations.rule: Plowman’s text specifies that at the start of the indicated rounds you may plow a field for 1 Food; the plows are not free.

violations.quote: Baking Sheet off the table due to missing reed/fireplace engines
violations.rule: Baking Sheet only requires the Bake Bread action and grain; it does not require a Fireplace or Cooking Hearth

violations.quote: build reed fences around stables
violations.rule: Fences cost 1 Wood each; no reed is required to build fences

violations.quote: pairs with your 1-VP bonus at end
violations.rule: Sheep Well is worth 2 VP when played, not 1 VP

violations.quote: builds one free stable
violations.rule: Stable Master text: "When you play this card, you can immediately build exactly 1 stable for 1 wood." It is not free; it requires paying 1 Wood.

violations.quote: Clay Kneader lines up with your Plow Maker and Plowman by providing clay (and some wood) when you plow and sow
violations.rule: Clay Kneader grants 1 clay only after using a Grain Seeds or Vegetable Seeds action (sowing), not when you plow

violations.quote: multiple Stable-tagged cards (Shed Builder, Beer Stall, Shepherd's Whistle, Carpenter's Axe, Sheep Well)
violations.rule: Sheep Well’s text makes no reference to stables—it only places food based on the number of sheep you have.

violations.quote: Patch Caregiver … by supplying vegetables or grain when you plow fields via Plow Maker/Plowman
violations.rule: Patch Caregiver’s effect triggers when you play the card, letting you buy 1 grain for 1 food or 1 vegetable for 3 food—it does not depend on plowing fields.

violations.quote: ensures you can pay the 2-food cost on the Major Improvement action for 4 food
violations.rule: There is no 2-food cost to take a Major Improvement action; you only pay the resource cost of the Major Improvement itself.

violations.quote: Kindling Gatherer will trigger on any food you gain—especially from Archway—and net you an extra wood
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only on food from an action space, not on all food gains (card text: “Each time you get food from an action space, you get 1 additional wood.”)

violations.quote: "Alchemists Lab provides a guaranteed influx of wood, clay, reed, and stone—resources you need for rooms and fields—each time you use its action"
violations.rule: Card text says you get 1 building resource of each type you already have, not necessarily all four resources if you don’t already have them.

violations.quote: "It fills the plow dimension before the Plow action appears on the board"
violations.rule: Farmland (Plow action) is always available on the main board from round 1, so the Plow action already exists.

violations.quote: Early game picks offer some food from Shifting Cultivation and action spaces, but no scalable engine yet
violations.rule: Shifting Cultivation does not provide any food; it only allows you to immediately plow one field (Minor Improvement “Shifting Cultivation”: “Immediately plow 1 field”).

violations.quote: Shifting Cultivation and Kindling Gatherer improve action efficiency but don’t add extra actions
violations.rule: Shifting Cultivation grants a free plow action when played, so it does add an extra action (Minor Improvement “Shifting Cultivation”: “Immediately plow 1 field”).

violations.quote: Shifting Cultivation ensures field presence and future support from Mole Plow
violations.rule: Mole Plow only triggers when you use the Farmland or Cultivation action space, not when plowing via a card effect like Shifting Cultivation.

violations.quote: conditional picks like Freemason that rely on having exactly two rooms in stone
violations.rule: Freemason works in either a clay or a stone house with exactly two rooms; it is not limited to stone houses.

violations.quote: boosts every future improvement play
violations.rule: Wood Carrier’s effect triggers only when you play Wood Carrier, giving you 1 wood per improvement you already have; it does not give wood on future improvement plays.

violations.quote: Combines with Bonehead and Kindling Gatherer to turn every cultivation or Grain Seeds turn into bonus wood.
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer only triggers when you get food from an action space (not on Cultivation or Grain Seeds), and Bonehead triggers only on playing cards, not on action use. They do not give wood on Cultivation or Grain Seeds turns.

violations.quote: Converts grain into 5 food at every harvest
violations.rule: Market Stall requires you to pay 1 grain AND 1 fence from your supply after each harvest’s field phase; it does not convert grain alone.

violations.quote: Corn Scoop, which only grants modest one-time grain bonuses
violations.rule: Corn Scoop’s text: “Each time you use the 'Grain Seeds' action space, you get 1 additional grain.” This is a repeatable effect, not a one-time bonus.

violations.quote: Bonehead, Kindling Gatherer, Shifting Cultivation, and Mole Plow providing multiple free plows and a wood-production backbone
violations.rule: Bonehead’s text grants wood on card play but does not grant any plow actions

violations.quote: Bonehead, Kindling Gatherer, Shifting Cultivation, and Mole Plow providing multiple free plows and a wood-production backbone
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer’s text triggers on food from an action space and does not grant any plow actions

violations.quote: Delivers an immediate 3 food boost which triggers Kindling Gatherer for 3 wood
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer only triggers from food gained via an action space; Blade Shears gives food on card play, not from an action space

violations.quote: each harvest feeding converts wood+grain into 2 food (triggering wood gains) and 1 VP
violations.rule: Kindling Gatherer triggers only when you get food from an action space; feeding-phase food comes outside of an action space and so does not trigger Kindling Gatherer.

violations.quote: one Big House (Family Friendly Home) tag
violations.rule: There is no “Big House” tag or card in Agricola; Family Friendly Home is the card’s name and effect, not a Big House tag

violations.quote: lack guaranteed access to Food/Grain accumulation spaces
violations.rule: There is no Grain accumulation space in Agricola; Grain Seeds is a fixed-yield space, not an accumulation space

violations.quote: rewarding accumulation actions (wood, stone, grain) with clay and boars
violations.rule: Mud Wallower gives clay only when you use any accumulation space, but there is no Grain accumulation space, so you cannot earn clay from grain

violations.quote: Small Greenhouse, which depends on vegetables
violations.rule: Small Greenhouse does not require you to have vegetables to play or activate; it places vegetables on future round spaces and lets you buy them for food, but it does not depend on existing vegetables

violations.quote: Family Friendly Home plus Adoptive Parents provide consistent extra Family Growth actions
violations.rule: Adoptive Parents grants an action with the offspring, not a “Family Growth” action (it allows taking an action with the newborn but does not grant the Family Growth action)

violations.quote: No cards yet producing extra actions after round placement

violations.quote: Young Animal Market leverages Dolly's Mother by converting your early sheep breed into a free cattle, boosting your animal scoring without additional actions

violations.quote: Field Watchman and Hill Cultivator ensure free plowing from Grain Seeds space

violations.quote: (1) Generates clay and boar passively each round, providing key building resources without any prerequisites

violations.quote: Pickler emphasizing Grain Seeds and Vegetable Seeds

violations.quote: delivers immediate wood instead of deferred benefit

violations.quote: (2) Fills your growth gap by giving an extra family member once you have a stone room adjacent to a field and pasture.
violations.rule: Homekeeper does not grant a new family member; it only increases the capacity of one room—it does not trigger Family Growth.

violations.quote: (1) Provides 1 food at the start of each round without requiring extra actions

violations.quote: Rewards your first 5th family member with 8 food, synergizing with cheap renovation from Chimney Sweep to free up actions for growth

violations.quote: Estate Worker and Field Cultivator provide passive resources and occasional actions

violations.quote: Sheep Whisperer synergizes with Fodder Planter and Animal Husbandry Worker by creating newborn sheep that trigger free sow actions and capitalize on your pasture-building.
